Take Action

The manifesto is a demand. Your action makes it real.

Whether you are an individual, an organisation, a practitioner, or a researcher — there is something concrete you can do right now.

For Individuals

Add your voice

Sign the pledge

Add your name to the growing list of people who support the Black Mental Health Manifesto and its 23 recommendations for structural change.

Your data will be handled in accordance with our privacy policy.

Thank you — your name is on the list. Now share the manifesto with one person who should read it.

Share the manifesto

Four ready-to-post graphics — tap to download, post, and tag the Alliance.

Prefer words? Copy this email for your networks — and the key facts make ready talking points.

Subject: The Black Mental Health Manifesto — will you back it?

I want to share something with you. Black people are detained under the Mental Health Act at 3.6 times the rate of white people, and only 6% of Black adults receive treatment for mental health problems, compared with 13% of White British adults. The Black Mental Health Manifesto sets out 23 evidence-based recommendations to end this — written by and for Black communities.

Read it at www.bmhwa.co.uk. If it speaks to you: sign the pledge, share it with your networks, and if you are part of an organisation, consider endorsing it. This is how structural change starts.

Write to your MP

Your elected representative needs to hear from you. Mental health reform, equitable funding for Black-led organisations, and the implementation of manifesto recommendations are all issues your MP can act on.

Use WriteToThem.com to find and write to your MP. Here is a suggested opening:

Dear [MP name],

I am writing to ask you to support the recommendations in the Black Mental Health Manifesto, published by the Black Mental Health and Wellbeing Alliance. Black people are detained under the Mental Health Act at nearly four times the rate of white people, yet only 6% receive treatment compared to 13% of White British adults. The Manifesto sets out 23 evidence-based recommendations to close this inequity gap. I urge you to read it and champion its demands in Parliament.

Find your MP on WriteToThem →

Endorse and implement

Implement recommendations

The manifesto is not just a statement — it is a practical framework. Use the 23 recommendations to audit your organisation’s policies, commissioning practices, and service delivery. Start with the recommendations most relevant to your role:

  • Commissioners & funders: Recommendations 6, 7, 12 — equitable funding, ICS priorities, community research
  • NHS Trusts: Recommendations 9, 14, 15 — PCREF, anti-racist practice, regulatory accountability
  • Local authorities: Recommendations 2, 8, 22, 23 — social prescribing, advocacy, school curriculum, exclusions
  • Voluntary sector: Recommendations 6, 13, 19 — sustainable funding, lived experience, culturally responsive interventions
Read all 23 recommendations
